shouldFix.title: The adoption drift guard omits the eight authored v8 fixture files
location: Measured inputs and remasurement clause, D-247 lines 84-120
shouldFix.claimUnderReview: D-247 proposes to record g21-fixture-corpus.v8 as eight per-D-002-platform authored copies, but its adoption-time unmoved roster names corpus v8 and the two Stage A verdicts without naming the eight external fixture files that constitute those copies.
shouldFix.measurement: All eight files currently exist as distinct regular four-byte files at mode 0444 and link count 1. Each of the four length-prefix-0 copies hashes to df3f619804a92fdb4057192dc43dd748ea778adc52bc498ce80524c014b81119; each of the four prefix-one-over-prehandshake copies hashes to 76cc5805dab9b4eacefdb477f498020fd82bccdbc9c6a2d9ce10586ac85512b4. Those values equal the corresponding frozen v7 payload digests and the copies are byte-identical to the two v7 source files. Nevertheless, changing any one v8 fixture after this review would leave the frozen corpus, both frozen Stage A verdicts, and the D-247 draft at exactly their recorded digests. The D-247 draft does not itself name any of the eight paths in either Measured inputs or the explicit unmoved roster, so its direct adoption custody surface cannot distinguish that drift.
evidence: D-247 lines 143-170 make the eight physical copies the fact being recorded, rather than merely recording an abstract catalog schema.
The v8 catalog names all eight external paths and their payload digests; freezing the catalog preserves those assertions, not the later live bytes at those paths.
D-247 lines 113-120 explicitly guard file 08, leftover joins, three occupancy artifacts, corpus v1 through v8, both Stage A verdicts, and the draft, but omit the eight v8 fixture files.
The exact earlier per-D-002-platform-copy decision D-243 closes this same drift window by requiring 'the eight v2 fixture files' to remain unmoved before adoption.
The current live-byte audit passes, so the defect is prospective adoption custody rather than a false payload or platform claim in the present draft.
shouldFix.impact: Without an explicit adoption-time freeze of the payload targets, a later adoption can durably record authored copies whose live bytes no longer match the reviewed catalog while every artifact explicitly named in D-247's unmoved roster still matches. The present bytes, Stage A result, platform provenance, leftover partition, readiness effect, and authority boundaries are all sound, so this is a localized recording-custody defect and SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX.
shouldFix.requiredRemedy: In a successor D-247 draft, add 'the eight v8 fixture files named in authoredCatalog' to the explicit unmoved roster and require remasurement before adoption if any one moves. The draft may also enumerate their eight path/digest pairs in Measured inputs, but the narrow repair is the explicit aggregate freeze used by D-243.
shouldFix.doesNotRequire: No change to g21-fixture-corpus.v8, either Stage A review, any fixture byte, fixtures/g21.v7/, leftover-join.v11, a predecessor corpus, file 08, live COORD, required-now 28, SATISFIED standing, Class A, QUALIFIED standing, leftoverDesign, or implementation authority is required.
